snip.t: In anaemia of chronic disease iron is locked in stores by hepcidin, so serum iron and transferrin saturation are low or normal, not raised.
snip.s: Internal Medicine End of Semester CAT (MBChB 4): haematology and renal, 30 MCQs

snip.t: Absorption is up‑regulated by low hepcidin. — In iron‑deficiency anaemia, ferritin is low and transferrin saturation falls; the student should explain why oral iron works only when hepcidin is suppressed.
In anaemia of chronic disease the transferrin saturation is increased.
snip.s: Hematology IMED Paper – Year 4 Internal Medicine

snip.t: Is typically a mild to moderate normocytic, normochromic, hypo-proliferative anemia associated with a decreased serum iron and low transferrin saturation.

In inflammation (IL‑6 driven) hepcidin rises → iron sequestration → anaemia of chronic disease. — High ferritin with low transferrin saturation suggests functional iron deficiency; the examiner may ask how to differentiate from true iron deficiency.
Net effect: ↓ serum ferritin & transferrin saturation → ↓ iron delivered to marrow → impaired haemoglobin synthesis → microcytic, hypochromic red cells → anaemia.
Inadequate intake / loss / sequestration → ↓ plasma iron → ↓ transferrin saturation → ↓ marrow iron → ↓ haemoglobin → microcytic hypochromic anaemia.
